column1: # adp_codes.tsv - Apple Diagnostics / AHT reference codes (2013+ Macs). code<TAB>meaning<TAB>bench note
# From Apple's public reference-code list (support.apple.com "Apple Diagnostics reference codes", HT203747). Verify there if a code is missing.
# macOS 26+ on Apple silicon: the same codes come from Repair Assistant > Mac Resource Inspector (Cmd-D at startup options).

column3: Diagnostics passed. A pass does NOT clear intermittent faults - run it 2-3x hot if the complaint is intermittent.
Wi-Fi/BT card or its antenna/flex. On Apple silicon the card is on the logic board.
Not necessarily a fault - Wi-Fi off, no networks in range, or antenna disconnected. Retest near a router.
FaceTime camera / camera flex / display assembly.
USB controller/port - check for a stuck device or liquid damage at the port.
Wi-Fi/BT card or antenna. Often pairs with CNW codes.
Trackpad / trackpad flex (look for a swollen battery pushing it).
TB controller / USB-C port - liquid damage and bent pins first.
Logic board was replaced without the serial being written, or board-level damage. Not a hardware fault by itself.
Intel: SMC reset first (shut down, Shift-Ctrl-Option + power 10 s). Persisting = logic board.
Reinstall macOS / DFU revive (Apple silicon + T2) before condemning the board.
Fan not spinning / wrong RPM - fan, fan cable, or the sensor telling it to spin.
Removable RAM: reseat/swap modules one at a time. Onboard: logic board.
SMC/PMU - reset SMC (Intel); check charger + battery data with MacDiag.
Try a known-good Apple adapter AND cable before blaming the Mac.
Plug in the adapter and rerun - the test wants to see charging.
Battery connector / battery flex / dead battery. On a desktop: ignore.
Still working, capacity low - quote a battery.
Battery is not functioning normally - replace.
Card reader / logic board. Check for a card stuck inside.
SSD/HDD failing - back up first (see MacDiag SMART). Soldered SSD = logic board.
Recovery partition missing/damaged - use Internet Recovery (Option-Cmd-R) or DFU restore.
Display panel / cable / backlight. Test with an external monitor to split panel vs GPU.
GPU fault - logic board (Intel dGPU models: classic reflow/replace candidates).
